trickyParts: awaitReconciled's timeout could name a cause that is already fixed. reconcileFailure returns the first logged failure, which in the repair test is always the pre-repair 'peer offline' WARN. bus.Client.HookStall (internal/bus/nats.go:560-568) returns the stall and the error of the last run that failed, which is what blocks the reconcile at the moment of the timeout.

awaitHookFailure needs no stream read to know the servers accepted the start. The reconcile is the publisher's only hook and ConnectOwningStream registers it before any caller can add one (internal/bus/nats.go:423, 532-538), so HookedConnectionEvents() >= 1 says the hooks ran through.
deviations: The worker also corrected awaitHookFailure's doc clause 'It fails the test when the stream reconciles instead' to 'when the start's hooks run through instead'.
